trust_decision.summary: The decision is which directory object a login or group-details request is about: the request-supplied user or group name is concatenated raw into the ADO command text "<LDAP://DC>;(sAMAccountName=<name>);distinguishedName;subTree" at ActiveDirectoryAuthenticationProvider.java:332 (Windows ADSI/COM implementation only), so the LDAP search filter is decided by the requester, not by the service.

landing_point.why: It is the only hand-built LDAP filter string in the tree; every other search passes the value as a JNDI {0} argument (LDAPSearchBuilder.java:120), which the JDK escapes, so an engineer hunting for a concatenated filter ends here.

fix_sites.module_kind: Jenkins SecurityRealm authentication provider (Windows ADSI/COM implementation of the two implementations the plugin ships)

fix_sites.entry_point: new static helper escapeLdapFilterValue, reached only from the line 332 call site
fix_sites.module_kind: new utility method in the same class

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 or O8 site exists to argue away: both public routes (login/user lookup and group details) funnel through the single private getDnOfUserOrGroup, so the only dismissal on offer is that ADSI mode itself is a Windows-only legacy path (the plugin prints 'Using Windows ADSI. No diagnostics available.' at ActiveDirectorySecurityRealm.java:451).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legit logins for user@domain (UPN), user.name and DOMAIN\user names must keep passing through unchanged, the DN->LDAP-URL conversion deliberately must not be double-escaped, and the ';' delimiters of the ADO command text must stay intact; an over-broad fix that escapes the DN or the naming context, that rewrites the whole command text, that rejects names containing '@' or '\', or that adds escaping to the JNDI {0} arguments (already escaped by DirContext.search) breaks binds and lookups for existing accounts.

O6_input_shapes: plain String username from the login/web path
plain String group name from the group-details path
null name (helper returns an empty string)
values containing each RFC 4515 metacharacter: backslash, asterisk, open paren, close paren, NUL (including an already-escaped-looking input such as a literal \2a)
benign names such as user.name and user@domain that must be unchanged

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ADO commandText filter in the same method, e.g. the userPrincipalName-then-sAMAccountName fallback pair the Unix implementation has
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the plugin ships two implementations of the same lookup and keeps the Windows one in step with the Java one (README.md:10-14); ActiveDirectoryUnixAuthenticationProvider.java:385,390 already shows the two-search shape, so a maintainer adding the UPN fallback to ADSI mode would hand-build a second filter and need the same escaping there

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a cn fallback before the sAMAccountName lookup inside loadGroupByGroupname, mirroring the group search order of the Unix implementation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ActiveDirectoryUnixAuthenticationProvider.java:528,534 does (cn) then (sAMAccountName) for groups; porting that order into the ADSI provider is a natural maintainer change and would add another raw concatenation of the group name

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller that formats the name into the filter string itself instead of passing it as a {0} argument to search()/searchOne()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the builder takes an arbitrary filter string, so nothing in its API prevents a caller from concatenating; a refactor of one of the four search sites could drop the argument form and silently lose the JDK's escaping

O9_family: LDAP injection (CWE-90): unescaped filter value concatenated into a directory search filter

O10_build.toolchain: Maven with the Jenkins plugin parent 5.24, hpi packaging, jenkins.version 2.504.3, .mvn/maven.config adding the incremental profiles
services: Maven artifact repository reachable over the network at build time (dependencies not vendored)
an Active Directory domain controller (Samba AD container or a domain-joined Windows host with COM4J) to exercise the affected path at runtime
O10_build.project_tests: ActiveDirectoryAuthenticationProviderTest.java is a plain unit test but at the pinned commit covers only dnToLdapUrl (no escaping test); the ADSI-mode coverage is Windows-only ITs that skip elsewhere (WindowsAdsiModeUserCacheDisabledIT.java:29 assumeTrue(isWindows()), same in WindowsAdsiModeUserCacheEnabledIT.java:31) and needs a domain-joined host with a pre-created user; the Samba AD end-to-end tests are Testcontainers-based and skip without Docker (RequireDockerRule.java:24).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the * ( and ) characters at the single commandText call (typically with a regex) and stop, leaving the literal backslash that re-introduces wildcard injection through a \2a sequence and the NUL character unhandled.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but outside this advisory: ActiveDirectoryUnixAuthenticationProvider.java:366 passes the user-supplied principal name as the LDAP bind name; that is a bind, not a search filter, and was not pursued.
unverified: The ADO LDAP dialect is '<LDAP://server>;filter;attributes;scope', so ';' is a component separator that the published escaper does not map; whether a name containing ';' can still break out of the filter component cannot be checked without a live Windows ADO/AD stack.

Whether the grader can exercise this fix at all: getDnOfUserOrGroup is reachable only through COM4J/ADO, and the provider is selected only when canDoNativeAuth() is true, which returns false unless the host is Windows (ActiveDirectorySecurityRealm.java:526-527, 949-956); no offline unit test on Linux can reach the sink, so a hidden behavioural test would have to target a solver-chosen helper by name or rely on a refactor.
Repository size in megabytes was not measured (no shell in this session); src/main/java is 4,403 lines across 26 files, which is the basis for the tiny_repo flag.
The advisory text itself was not supplied (only the one-line summary), so its exact wording about affected modes and scope could not be compared with the diff.
